titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 147, the seven gates, part 1
part: Spell 147 — the seven gates: the first three gates (Plate 11)
about: Spell 147 takes the dead man through the gates (ꜥryt) of the realm of Osiris. Each gate has three beings, a doorkeeper, a watcher and an announcer, whose names the dead man must know, and a speech he says on arriving. On Ani's papyrus the spell runs along the upper register of Plate 11; this part gives the first three gates, and Budge numbers the lines afresh in each gate. The copy is careless in places, and many of the names and some phrases are doubtful.

sentences.i: The first gate.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these two words in red. ꜥryt 'gate' is the arm ꜥ, r, two reeds y and t, with the house sign as classifier (Budge: ārit, 'hall'). In the address to the gods the same word names a part of a door, a lintel; here, with the house sign, it is a whole gate, a gatehouse on the way into the realm of Osiris. tpyt 'first' is the head tp with its stroke: tpy, the nisba adjective from tp 'head', which serves as the ordinal 'first', feminine to agree with ꜥryt; its endings are not written here, and in line 3 the same two words are written again with p and t. Spell 147 begins here, on the upper register of Plate 11, and this unit opens the first gate (ārit). Budge starts his line numbers again at 1 in each gate, so the first gate runs over his lines 1 to 17. Each gate has a doorkeeper, a watcher and an announcer, whose names the dead man must know before he can pass, and a speech he says on arriving.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Sekhed-her-asha-iru.
sentences.n: rn 'name' is r and n with the man with hand to mouth (coded A2), the classifier; n 'of' is water n, restored by Budge inside his square brackets. iry-ꜥꜣ·s 'its doorkeeper' is the seated herdsman with his stick (A47), standing for iry 'keeper' (Budge: àri), and an upright hatched sign coded O29 (approximate; it may be the door-leaf O31), giving ꜥꜣ 'door': iry-ꜥꜣ, 'the one who belongs to the door'. Then the low sign coded U15, not read, and the bolt ·s 'its', the gate's. The sentence has no verb: 'the name of X (is) Y'. The name is two of Budge's groups, joined here as one word. sḫd-ḥr is the folded cloth s, the placenta ḫ, the hand d, a sign not identified (coded T26, approximate: a cone on a stem between two legs) taken as classifier, and the face ḥr with its stroke. ꜥšꜣ-irw is the lizard ꜥšꜣ 'many', then a reed, the eye ir and w, with a mummy figure, the roll and a stroke: irw 'forms'. If sḫd is the verb 'be upside down', the name means 'Upside-down of face, many of forms' (Budge: Seχeṭ-ḥrà-āśt-àru). The first half rests on that guess and on a sign not identified, and is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its watcher: Metety-he(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn in red; the rest is black. sꜣwty·s 'its watcher' is the herdsman with his stick, here with his own value sꜣw 'guard', two reeds y, t and two strokes y, the low sign U15 and the bolt ·s: the nisba sꜣwty 'guardian, watcher', its y written twice, once before the t. Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside the word. The name is the phallus mt (D53) with t, a second t and two strokes y, the eye, and a sign coded V28 (approximate: the type shows a tall loop with a small bulb at its foot, a shape that suits the shelter h as well as the wick ḥ). Budge reads Metti-heh. The eye is taken here as a classifier and not read, and the last sign is read ḥ: mtty-ḥ. The name is not understood, and its end depends on that uncertain sign.

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Ha-kheru.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. smi 'announcer' is the folded cloth s, the lung-and-windpipe sign smꜣ (F36) standing for sm, a reed i and the man with hand to mouth: smi 'report, announce', used as a noun for the one who announces whoever arrives (Budge: semà). im·s 'in it' is the reed and the owl, the form of m before a suffix, with ·s. The name hꜣ-ḫrw is the shelter h with ꜣ and walking legs, and the oar ḫrw 'voice' with w and the man with hand to mouth (Budge: Ha-χeru). hꜣ with walking legs is 'go down', so perhaps 'Descending of voice'; the meaning is doubtful.

sentences.l: said · by · Ani · true-of-voice · when · arriving · at · gate · first
sentences.i: Said by Ani, true of voice, on arriving at the first gate:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red, Ani's name and the words up to r in black, and ꜥryt tpt in red again. ḏd in N 'said by N' introduces the speech, as before: ḏd is the cobra and the hand (printed as one sign) with a stroke and plural strokes (Budge reads t'eṭtu, taking the strokes as the passive ḏd·tw 'it is said'; the sense is the same), and in is the reed with the sign coded W25 (approximate), as the house reads it. Ani's name ends here in a squatting man holding a flail (coded A52), the person classifier; mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' as before, the plinth and the oar without the sickle. The title has Ani, not 'the Osiris Ani'. ḫft 'when, at the time of' is the placenta ḫ, the horned viper f and t, a preposition before the infinitive spr 'arriving', the rib spr (F42) with r and walking legs. r 'at'. ꜥryt tpyt 'the first gate', here with the head, p and t; the y of tpyt is not written.

sentences.i: I am the great one who makes his light.
sentences.n: The speech begins. ink 'I' is the pot and the basket with the seated man; ink with a noun makes a sentence without a verb, 'I am …'. wr 'the great one' is the swallow wr with r and a seated god as classifier: the adjective used as a noun. ir, the eye alone, is the participle of iri 'do, make', 'who makes'. sšp·f 'his light' is the sign šsp (coded O42, approximate: a curved roof with hatching) with p and the sun, and ·f: sšp 'light, brightness'. The signs give šsp; the s of sšp is not written, as in Spell 22 (Budge: seśep). The speaker claims to be the being who brings his own light, like the sun.

sentences.i: I have come to you, Osiris.
sentences.n: ii·n·i is the sign ii (M18) with a reed and walking legs, then water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f of ii 'come', 'I have come'. ḫr·k 'to you' is ḫ and r with ·k, the preposition ḫr, used of persons. wsir is the eye and the throne with the seated god, as often on this papyrus.

sentences.i: I adore you, cleansed of your efflux.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes r, an oblong sign coded N37 (approximate: flat, with two diagonal strokes), w, a sign coded Aa2, plural strokes and ·k (Budge: ertu-k); read rḏw·k 'your efflux', the fluid that runs from a corpse. Budge's footnote gives the word with the mountain ḏw (N26), a coil w, Aa2 and grains, and the oblong is taken for the mountain. dwꜣ·i is the star dwꜣ with a standing man with one arm raised (coded A30, approximate) and the roll, and the seated man ·i: 'I adore'. tw 'you' is the dependent pronoun, t and w. wꜥb is the leg under a jet of water (D60), the sign of wꜥb 'be pure', with three water lines (Budge reads āb): a stative or participle, 'pure, cleansed', with no ending written, so the signs do not show whether the speaker or Osiris is the pure one. It is taken as the speaker, made clean of the decay of the dead god's body before he approaches it. r 'from'.

sentences.l: draw-on-(me) · not-you · make · the-name · of · Rosetau · against-him
sentences.i: Draw me on! You are not to make the name of Rosetau against him(?).
sentences.n: sṯꜣ is the folded cloth s, t, a tall pot coded W10 (approximate), ꜣ, the cord sign sṯꜣ (V2) and walking legs. The pot stands where štꜣ 'hidden' has the kiln tꜣ in Spell 17, and it is read tꜣ here; the cord and the legs are classifiers. It is the imperative of sṯꜣ 'drag, draw along', with t for ṯ: 'draw (me) on' (Budge: sta). im·k is a reed, the owl m and ·k: taken as the negative verb imi with its suffix, before irt, the eye with r, t and plural strokes, 'you are not to make'; after imi the verb would take its negatival complement, and irt, with its t, looks rather like the infinitive, which adds to the doubt. rn n rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'the name of Rosetau', the realm of the dead of Sokar near Memphis: the mouth rꜣ with a stroke, the cord sṯꜣ (approximate), strokes and the desert sign. r·f is r with ·f, 'against him' or 'to him'; it could also be the particle rf 'then'. Who is spoken to, and what making the name of Rosetau means, are not clear; the sentence is doubtful.

morph.gloss: do not …, you are not to … (the negative verb imi, with a suffix and the negatival complement of the next verb)

sentences.l: hail-face-your · Osiris · in · power-your · in · strength-your · in · Rosetau
sentences.i: Hail to you, Osiris, in your power and in your strength in Rosetau!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ind-ḥr·k in red. It is a reed, the sign nḏ (coded Aa27, approximate) and the cobra ḏ arched over the face ḥr and its stroke, and ·k: the greeting ind ḥr·k, literally 'greetings to your face', 'hail to you'. m 'in' is written first with the sign Aa15, then twice with the owl. sḫm·k 'your power' is the sceptre sḫm (S42) with a stroke and plural strokes, and ·k. wsr·k 'your strength' is the head and neck of an animal, wsr (F12), with s and r, the low sign U15 and plural strokes, and ·k. rꜣ-sṯꜣw as before; its second writing falls in line 6.

sentences.l: raise · yourself · have-power-may-you · Osiris · in · Abydos
sentences.i: Raise yourself; may you have power, Osiris, in Abydos!
sentences.n: Budge's group θes-tu is split here into ṯs and tw. ṯs is a hairpin sign coded V13 (approximate) for ṯ, the bolt s, and a forked post (coded S24, approximate) and the low sign U15 as classifiers: the imperative of ṯs 'raise', with tw, the dependent pronoun, t and w, 'raise yourself'. sḫm·k is the sceptre with m and ·k: a sḏm·f used as a wish, 'may you have power'. Budge's footnote says that the papyrus itself has a reed, the owl and the basket here, im·k, not the sceptre: the sceptre in his type is his own correction, made from sḫm·k in the line before, and not what Ani's scribe wrote. The signs are kept as Budge prints them and his sḫm·k is followed, with that warning; with the papyrus's im·k the words would be 'raise yourself … in you(?)', which makes no clear sense. A faint mark stands before m. ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is the sign coded S34 (the house ruling for ꜣb) with b, the mountain ḏw and the town sign. Abydos is the town of Osiris's tomb, where the dead god is told to rise.

sentences.i: You go round the sky, you sail upstream before Ra.
sentences.n: rr·k is a long closed loop (coded V10, approximate, as in Spell 17), r and walking legs, and ·k: the verb rr 'go round', a sḏm·f, 'you go round'. pt 'the sky' is p and t with the sky sign. ḫnt·k is a tall stand crossed by a stick (coded W17, approximate) for ḫnt, with n and a boat (coded P1, approximate) as classifier, and ·k: ḫnti 'sail upstream'. Then come t and w, tw, which Budge leaves untranslated: perhaps the dependent pronoun, 'yourself', after a verb of motion, or a stray; it is not rendered. ḫft 'before' is the placenta, the horned viper and t, as in line 3; rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun on his head. The risen Osiris crosses the sky with the sun.

sentences.i: You have seen all the common folk.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes nb in red. mꜣꜣ·n·k is the eye joined with the sickle mꜣ (U1) in one sign, the sickle giving the sound and the eye the classifier, then water n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f of mꜣꜣ 'see', 'you have seen'. rḫyt 'the common folk' is the lapwing with t and plural strokes. nb 'all' is the basket, after its noun; the feminine ending that rḫyt would take is not written.

sentences.i: O, Ra has gone round in it(?)!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i rr·n in red; rꜥ im·s are black. i 'O' is the reed with the man with hand to mouth. rr·n is the long loop, r and walking legs, the verb of line 6, with water n. Budge's groups rer and en are joined here into one word: the sḏm·n·f with the noun rꜥ as its subject, 'Ra has gone round'. im·s 'in it' has the feminine pronoun; 'it' may be the sky (pt) or the gate. The words could also be a relative form, 'O you whom Ra has gone round in it'. The sentence is doubtful.

sentences.i: See, I say, Osiris:
sentences.n: mk 'see, behold' is the owl m and the basket k, with the arm between them (printed as one sign with the owl), not read; earlier parts write the word with the arm too. ḏd·i 'I say' is the cobra and the hand with the seated man ·i. wsir as before: the speaker turns to the god again.

sentences.i: I am a divine noble: I have spoken, and it comes about.
sentences.n: ink 'I am' again. sꜥḥ 'noble, dignitary' is the bolt s, the arm ꜥ and the wick ḥ, with a loop on a T-shaped stand (coded S34, approximate; not a clear ankh) and the seated god as classifiers. nṯr 'god' is the flag with the seated god, after its noun: 'a noble of god', 'a divine noble'. ḏd·n·i is the sḏm·n·f of ḏd, 'I have said', and ḫpr is the scarab ḫpr with r, a sḏm·f, 'it comes about'. Budge's numeral 8 stands before nṯr, and 9 between ḏd·n·i and ḫpr. Read together, 'I have spoken, and it comes about' is the claim of a creator whose word takes effect. Budge takes ḫpr with what follows, 'let it be that …'.

sentences.l: not · opposing · against-me · at-it · at · wall-his · of-burning-coals
sentences.i: There is no opposing me at it, at his wall of burning coals.
sentences.n: n is the arms held out (D35; the type shows a line with a central hump) with water n: the negative, 'there is no', before ḫsf, the spindle-and-viper sign ḫsf (U35) with the low sign U15 and a stroke, the infinitive 'opposing, driving back'. r·i 'against me' is r and the seated man ·i, both restored by Budge inside his square brackets. ḥr·s 'at it' is the face with its stroke and the bolt ·s, 'it' being the gate. inb·f 'his wall' is a reed, the fish in (K1) with n, b and the wall sign (O36), and the horned viper ·f. Budge prints the wall at the start of his next row and the viper after his numeral 12, rendering it 'of'; his groups àneb and -f are joined here into one word. The ·f is masculine, so the wall is not the gate's but 'his', perhaps the god's. ḏꜥbt 'charcoal, burning coals' is the cobra ḏ, the arm ꜥ, b and t, with grains and plural strokes, a noun after a noun: 'a wall of coals', a ring of fire round the gate.

sentences.l: opening · the-way · in · Rosetau · easing · the-pain · of-Osiris
sentences.i: Opening the way in Rosetau, easing the pain of Osiris,
sentences.n: wp is the horns wp (F13) alone: taken as the infinitive of wpi 'open', its t not written, the first of a list of deeds in the infinitive that runs to the end of the speech (Budge supplies 'I have'). The t of irt in line 17 shows the infinitive; the third gate tells the same deeds with the sḏm·n·f, 'I have opened … I have eased', and these bare forms could be read so too, with n and the suffix unwritten. wꜣt 'the way' is the road sign with t and a stroke; m 'in' (Aa15); rꜣ-sṯꜣw as before. snḏm is the folded cloth s, a twisted sign coded V28 (approximate), m, and the roll with a stroke: snḏm 'ease, soothe', the causative of nḏm 'be sweet'. The twisted sign is taken as standing for the sign nḏm, and the reading rests on that (Budge reads senet'em, with no ḥ). mn 'pain' is the gaming board mn with n and the bird of bad things. wsir is the throne and the eye, the noun after mn making the genitive, 'the pain of Osiris'. The infinitives tell what the speaker has done for the god.

sentences.i: embracing(?) the one who judges(?) the standard,
sentences.n: sḫn is the folded cloth s, ḫ and n, with two embracing arms (coded D32, approximate) as classifier: sḫn 'embrace', an infinitive like those before (Budge: seχen). nty 'the one who' is n, t and two strokes. wḏꜥ is the sign wḏꜥ (Aa21) with the roll: wḏꜥ 'judge, separate'. No subject is written after it, so it is not a regular sḏm·f after nty (which would need its own subject); the form is unclear, and 'who judges' takes nty as its subject. iꜣt is a reed, ꜣ and t with a beam on a post with a brace (coded R12, approximate) as classifier: iꜣt 'standard', the pole that carries a god's emblem. The sense of the clause is not clear: 'embracing the one who judges the standard' follows the words as they stand, and wḏꜥ may have another sense here.

sentences.l: making · way-his · in · the-valley · great · making · the-way
sentences.i: making his way in the great valley, making the way.
sentences.n: irt is the eye with t and a stroke, the infinitive of iri 'make'; wꜣt·f 'his way' has ·f. m 'in'. int 'valley' is a reed, the fish in with n, t and the desert sign. wr is the swallow with r: 'great', after its noun. The feminine ending that int would need is not written, and Budge takes wr as a separate 'great one'. irt wꜣt 'making the way' again; the eye and the t of irt are Budge's restoration inside his square brackets.

sentences.i: The light of Osiris(?).
sentences.n: sšp 'light' is the sign šsp with p and the sun, as in line 3. Then come water n and t, over which Budge prints '(sic)': taken as nt 'of', the genitive in its feminine form, which does not agree with sšp, followed by wsir (the eye and the throne with the god). Budge reads a sentence, 'Osiris shines'; with the verb sšp 'shine, be bright', the water n could also be the n of the sḏm·n·f, 'Osiris has shone', with the t left unexplained. The third gate's speech ends with sšp·f m rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'his light is in Rosetau', and this may be a shortened form of the same close. The end of the first gate's speech is doubtful.

sentences.i: The second gate.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these two words in red. This unit opens the second gate (ārit), and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the second gate runs over his lines 1 to 9. ꜥryt as at the first gate. snnwt 'second' is two strokes, the numeral two (sn), with the pot nw: the ordinal snnw, its feminine ending not written.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Wen-hat.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s as at the first gate: the herdsman sign for iry, the sign coded O29 for ꜥꜣ 'door', and ·s, here without the low sign U15. The name wn-ḥꜣt is the hare wn with n, a hatched door-leaf hanging from a line (O31) as classifier of opening, the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt (F4) with t and a stroke, and the seated god (Budge: Un-ḥāt). wn 'open' and ḥꜣt 'front, brow' are clear, so the name may mean 'Open of front', but how the two words go together is not.

sentences.i: The name of its watcher: Seqed-her.
sentences.n: Here no n 'of' is written: rn stands directly before its noun, the direct genitive, 'the name of'. sꜣwty·s 'its watcher' as at the first gate, here with ꜣ written. Its final bolt ·s is restored by Budge inside square brackets that also hold the first sign of the name. The name is the bolt s (restored), a tall thin wedge coded N29 (approximate; the thorn M44 is the other possible shape) for q, the hand d with the pot nw under it, not read, and the face ḥr with its stroke and the seated god. Budge's numeral 4 stands inside it. sqd is 'travel by boat', so 'Voyaging of face' is possible but a guess. The name is given as Seqed-her (Budge: Seqeṭ-ḥrà).

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Used.
sentences.n: rn n smi im·s as at the first gate. The name wsd is w, the folded cloth s and the hand d, with a blade (coded T30, approximate), the low sign U15 and the seated god as classifiers (Budge: Useṭ). It is not understood; the classifiers point to a word of cutting or force.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani at this (gate):
sentences.n: ḏd in N 'said by N' as at the first gate, here in black, with in written as a reed and water n. wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani', the dead man named as an Osiris: the throne and the eye, and Ani's name with the seated man. Then the papyrus writes tn 'this' in red, t and water n: the feminine demonstrative, which stands after its noun, but the noun is not written. It is taken as 'this (gate)', what is left of 'on arriving at this gate', with the rest left out; Budge supplies the arrival in brackets.

sentences.l: sits-he · at · doing · the-head · in · intent · judging · speech · as · the-second · of-Thoth
sentences.i: He sits to do the chief thing(?) in intention(?), judging speech as the second of Thoth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḥms·f … wḏꜥ in red, though the words belong to the speech. ḥms·f is a figure seated with knees raised (coded A7, approximate) for ḥms 'sit', and ·f: 'he sits'. ḥr with the infinitive irt, the eye and t, makes 'doing, to do'. tp 'head, chief' is the head with its stroke. ḫmt is ḫ, the phallus mt (D53), t, three strokes (coded Z3A) and the arms held out (D35): ḫmt 'think, intend', the strokes perhaps taken from ḫmt 'three' and the arms from ḫm 'not know'. 'Doing the chief thing in intention' is a guess at a phrase not understood. wḏꜥ, the sign Aa21 alone, is 'judging'. ḏdt 'speech' is a narrow tapering sign coded U28 (approximate, as ruled in Spell 1) for ḏ, the hand d and t, with the seated man and a stroke (Budge's numeral 7 inside it). m snnw ḏḥwty 'as the second of Thoth': snnw with the numeral two and the pot; ḏḥwty the ibis with t and two strokes. 'He' is not named: the god of the gate, or Osiris, whose deputy judges what is said, as Thoth records the judgement.

sentences.l: the-protection · of-Thoth · from · weariness · the-gods-of-Maat · hidden · who-live · on · maat · in · years-their
sentences.i: The protection of Thoth against(?) the weariness(?) of the hidden gods of Maat(?), who live on maat through their years.
sentences.n: mꜣꜥtyw 'the gods of Maat' is a guess: the word is the sickle mꜣ (U1) with the arm ꜥ and t, then ꜣ and n (Budge marks the n sic), the seated god and a stroke. The god classifier points to beings named from mꜣꜥt, but the ꜣ and the n are left unexplained (Budge: Maāta, 'the Maāta gods'). mkt is the owl m, the arm (not read, as in mk), the basket k and t, with the roll and a stroke: mkt 'protection' (Budge: māket); ḏḥwty after it makes the genitive. gḥ is a sign coded W11 (approximate: a trapezoid with a small triangle) for g, the wick ḥ and a standing man with arms hanging (coded A7, approximate): taken as gꜣḥ 'be weary, faint', its ꜣ not written; the standing man with arms hanging is the classifier of weariness (Budge: ḳeḥ). As an infinitive it can take the following noun as its subject, 'the weariness of …'. štꜣ 'hidden' is the oblong coded N37 for š, t, the pot coded W10 for tꜣ, ꜣ, the crossed sticks, the roll and a stroke. ꜥnḫyw 'who live' is the ankh with two reeds, w and a stroke, a plural participle; m mꜣꜥt 'on maat', with a feather (H6) and the roll; m rnpwt·sn 'in their years', the palm-rib rnp (M4) with t and plural strokes, and ·sn. Gods who 'live on maat' feed on right order. How the words go together is not clear, and the rendering is doubtful.

sentences.i: I am one who makes offering at the moment of making his way.
sentences.n: ink 'I am' with the seated man. wdn is w, the hand d and water n, with a narrow hairpin loop (coded V1, approximate) and a block (O39) as classifiers: wdn 'offer', a participle, 'one who offers'. ꜣt 'moment' is t and ꜣ, the t written first, with an animal's head (coded F3, the hippopotamus head that classifies this word). ir, the eye alone, is the infinitive 'making'; Budge prints 'àrit uat-f' as one group, split here into ir and wꜣt·f 'his way'. The nouns side by side make 'the moment of making his way', with 'at' supplied.

sentences.i: I tread on; I have made an embracing(?) of the way.
sentences.n: iw is the reed and w, opening a statement, and is not translated. ḫnd·i is ḫ, water n and the hand d with walking legs: ḫnd 'tread', a sḏm·f after iw, 'I tread'; the suffix ·i is not written, and Budge adds it in brackets in his transliteration only. ir·n·i is the eye with water n: the sḏm·n·f of iri, 'I have made', its suffix ·i again not written, as often on this papyrus. sḫn is the embracing arms (D32, approximate) alone, written for sḫn 'embrace' (Budge prints 'àri-nà seχen' as one group, split here into ir·n and sḫn). wꜣt 'the way'. The first person is read from the speech around it. The sense is doubtful.

sentences.l: give-may-you · pass-I · […] · seeing · Ra · with · those-who-make · offerings
sentences.i: May you grant that I pass and […] the sight of Ra with those who make offerings.
sentences.n: di·k is the giving arm di, rdi written with di alone, and ·k: a sḏm·f expressing a wish, 'may you give, grant'. swꜣ·i is the crossed sticks swꜣ (Z9) with walking legs and the seated man: 'that I may pass' (Budge: seś-à). sšd is a looped cord coded V6 (approximate), the hand d and the low sign U15, read sšd with Budge (seśeṭ) as though the cord were the sign sš; the word was left unidentified in Spell 17 and is not translated here. No ·i is written after it. mꜣꜣ 'seeing, the sight' is the eye joined with the sickle, and a stroke; rꜥ is a small curl (coded D21, approximate) and the sun. m-ꜥ 'with' is the owl and the arm. iryw 'those who make' is the eye, r, two reeds y, the coil w and a stroke, the plural participle of iri. ḥtpw 'offerings' is the offering table ḥtp with t and p, and a rounded loaf (coded X4, approximate).

sentences.i: The third gate.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these two words in red. This unit opens the third gate (ārit), and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the third gate runs over his lines 1 to 8. ꜥryt as before. ḫmtnwt 'third' is three short strokes (coded Z15B), the numeral three (ḫmt), and t: the ordinal ḫmtnw, written with the numeral and the feminine t only.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Qeq-huaut-net-pehuy.
sentences.n: iry-ꜥꜣ·s as at the first gate, with the low sign U15. The name is two of Budge's groups, joined here into one word. Two small triangles coded N29 give q and q, with the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of eating: qq 'eat'. The wick ḥ, ꜣ, the lasso wꜣ (coded V4, approximate), t and w, with a pustule (Aa2) and plural strokes, spell ḥwꜣwt 'putrefaction, rotting matter', related to ḥwꜣw 'rottenness'; its last three signs are printed after Budge's numeral 3. Then nt 'of', water n and t, the feminine genitive agreeing with ḥwꜣwt, and pḥwy 'hinder parts', the rump pḥ (F22) with w and two strokes. The name means 'Eater of the rot of the hindquarters' (Budge: Qeq-ḥauatu-ent-peḥui), a keeper with a name to repel anyone who comes near.

sentences.i: The name of its watcher: Seres-her.
sentences.n: sꜣwty·s 'its watcher' as before, with ꜣ but without the t, which is not written. The name is the bolt s, r, the folded cloth s, an upright with a forked top (coded T13, approximate) for rs 'wake', the eye, and the face ḥr with its stroke and the seated god (Budge's numeral 5 stands before the face). srs-ḥr, from srs 'awaken, make watchful', the causative of rs, would mean 'Who keeps the face awake', 'Watchful of face' (Budge: Se-res-ḥrà). The reading rests on the forked sign, an uncertain identification; the eye, as a classifier, suits a name of watching.

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Aa.
sentences.n: smi im·s 'the announcer in it' as before. The name is a hatched door-leaf hanging from a line (O31), the low sign U15, a block (O39) and the seated god: ꜥꜣ, written with the door-leaf, which writes ꜥꜣ 'door' (Budge: Āaa). It may mean 'the Great One' (ꜥꜣ 'great'), or play on 'door'; doubtful.

morph.gloss: Aa, the announcer of the third gate; perhaps 'the Great One' (name; written with the door-leaf; Budge: Āaa)

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red, and wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani' in black. ḏd in 'said by' as at the first gate, with in written as a reed and water n.

sentences.i: I am the hidden one of the deep, who judges between the Two Companions.
sentences.n: ink is the pot and the basket, here with a bold stroke in place of the seated man. štꜣ 'the hidden one' is written as at the second gate, with the crossed sticks and the roll (Budge's numeral 6 inside it). gb is the sign coded W11 (approximate) for g, b and three water lines: taken as qbb 'the cool waters, the deep', with g for q and one b (Budge: ḳeb); doubtful. The two nouns side by side make the genitive, and Budge supplies 'in'. wp is the horns wp with p: the participle of wpi 'judge between', 'who judges'. rḥwy 'the Two Companions' is r with a stroke, ḥ and w, with two seated gods for the dual: Horus and Seth, whose quarrel the speaker settles.

sentences.i: I have come to drive away the evil from Osiris.
sentences.n: ii·n·i is the sign ii with a reed, walking legs and water n, 'I have come', as at the first gate but without the seated man: the suffix ·i is not written, as often on this papyrus, and is read from the speaker's 'I' around it. dr·i is the hand d, r, the low sign U15 and the seated man: dr 'drive away', a sḏm·f of purpose, 'that I may drive away'. ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw with w and t and the bird of bad things. ḥr 'from' is the face with its stroke; wsir as before.

sentences.l: I · who-clothes · standard-his · coming-forth · from · the-Great-Crown
sentences.i: I am one who clothes his standard, which comes forth from the Great Crown.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣ, t and the sun (Budge prints '(sic)' beside it), the spelling of ꜣt 'moment', with the horned viper ·f after Budge's numeral 7; read iꜣt·f 'his standard', as in line 8. ink 'I am'. wnḫ is the hare wn with n and ḫ, then a looped cord (coded V6, approximate) and the low sign U15 as classifiers, both restored by Budge inside his square brackets: wnḫ 'clothe, dress', a participle, 'who clothes'. pr 'which comes forth' is the house with r and walking legs, the participle of pri. m 'from'. wrrt 'the Great Crown' is t, the swallow wr and r (one r written), the crown named from wr 'great'. The standard of Osiris was dressed in the rites at Abydos, and the crown is the god's.

sentences.i: I have set things in order in Abydos.
sentences.n: smnḫ·n·i is the bolt s, the gaming board mn with n, ḫ, a bell-shaped sign coded U22 (approximate; the chisel mnḫ) as classifier, then water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f of smnḫ 'make excellent, set in order', 'I have set in order' (Budge: semenχ-nà). ḫt 'things' is ḫ and t with the roll and plural strokes. m ꜣbḏw 'in Abydos', written here with w. The rites of Osiris at Abydos are meant.

sentences.i: I have opened the way in Rosetau;
sentences.n: wp·n is the horns wp with p, the crossed sticks and the roll, and water n: the sḏm·n·f of wpi 'open', 'I have opened', its suffix ·i not written (Budge: àp-nà). wꜣt m rꜣ-sṯꜣw as at the first gate, the same deed told here in the sḏm·n·f.

sentences.i: I have eased the pain in Osiris.
sentences.n: snḏm·n is the bolt s, the twisted sign coded V28 taken as nḏm (as at the first gate), m and water n: 'I have eased', its suffix ·i not written; Budge's numeral 8 follows the bolt. mnt 'pain' is mn with n, t and the bird of bad things (Budge marks the m in his transliteration). m wsir 'in Osiris': the pain is in the god's body.

sentences.i: I have […] his standard; I have made the way.
sentences.n: sḫḫ is the bolt s, ḫ twice and the roll: a word not known, given as the signs stand and not translated (Budge: seχeχ, 'made to balance'). No n of the sḏm·n·f is written; the English follows the clauses around it. iꜣt·f 'his standard' is a reed, ꜣ, t and the standard sign (coded R12, approximate) with ·f. ir·n·i 'I have made' is the eye, water n and the seated man; wꜣt 'the way'.

sentences.i: His light is in Rosetau.
sentences.n: sšp·f is the sign šsp with p and the sun (the s again not written), and ·f: 'his light', a noun with its suffix, as in the first gate. m rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'in Rosetau'. Read as a sentence without a verb, 'his light is in Rosetau'; it may also be the verb, 'he shines', as Budge takes it. The third gate ends here, and the fourth begins in the next part.
